title: World Cup sell off: Has FIFA finally gone too far?
first_paragraph: A new FIFA proposal to sell off a stake in the World Cup has been met with fury in the football world. Under Gianni Infantino’s presidency, FIFA has become increasingly profit-driven, but is this too much?

title: Germany news: Temperatures to soar amid new heatwave
first_paragraph: Germany is once again baking under extreme heat. Meanwhile, Chancellor Merz's Cabinet shake-up — triggered by a surrogacy scandal — was formalized in a series of ministerial appointments. DW has more.

title: BMW to cut up to 8,000 jobs
first_paragraph: Nearly half of BMW's German staff will receive a voluntary redundancy offer in the carmaker's bid to reduce staff by about 8,000 people.

title: Europe wildfires: Spain lets people return, France faces extreme heat
first_paragraph: Spain lifted evacuations for Avila province, a day after doing so in parts of the Madrid area. To the north in France, temperatures rose again, with extreme heat warnings in much of the country, including Gironde.

title: How a Ugandan lost 20 years of her life to xenophobia
first_paragraph: After decades of building lives in South Africa, renewed anti-immigrant tensions in 2026 forced hundreds of African migrants to leave. A Ugandan who spent two decades in South Africa shared with DW how she's coping.

title: Iran signals gas price hike as fuel crisis looms
first_paragraph: Iranian authorities want to dampen fuel consumption, but a sudden increase in gasoline prices risks social unrest as many Iranian households are already under severe economic pressure.

title: Lebanon's pilot zone plan: Can it work?
first_paragraph: The Israeli army has handed so-called "pilot zones" back to the Lebanese, The move is meant to facilitate an end to fighting between Hezbollah and Israel, and to Israeli occupation. But locals and experts are skeptical.

title: Bayreuth Festival: Ceremony and commemoration
first_paragraph: To mark its 150th anniversary, the Bayreuth Festival remembers victims of the Holocaust — and confronts its founder's antisemitism.

title: France: DJ Kavinsky found dead at Paris home
first_paragraph: The star of the French electro scene, whose real name was Vincent Belorgey, was best known for his 2010 single Nightcall which he performed at the closing ceremony of the 2024 Olympic Games in Paris.

title: Japan: Hospitals struggle after deadly Kumamoto earthquake
first_paragraph: Rescuers are searching for survivors after a magnitude 7.1 earthquake struck southern Japan, killing over a dozen people and causing widespread damage. DW has more.

title: Germany: How effective are exit programs for Islamists?
first_paragraph: Germany has set up many programs to help individuals break away from the radical Islamist scene. Following the Islamist terror attack on Berlin's Pride event, critics say the programs are ineffective.

title: India news: Police issue FIRs over 'abusive' posts against Modi
first_paragraph: Delhi police asked X to provide details on users who allegedly posted or shared "abusive" content on Prime Minister Narendra Modi. Follow DW for more.

title: US bans Chinese and foreign-made humanoid robots
first_paragraph: The Trump administration has banned the import of humanoid and quadruped robots manufactured outside the United States, citing national security concerns. The ban could strain diplomatic tensions with China.

title: How Iran, Ukraine wars and El Nino could fuel world hunger
first_paragraph: The wars in Ukraine and the Middle East haven't yet crippled global food supplies. Add a powerful weather pattern like El Nino, however, and the risks multiply.

title: The Slovak village questioning its UNESCO status
first_paragraph: The picturesque village of Vlkolinec in Slovakia has been on UNESCO's World Heritage List since 1993. Vlkolinec was recently in the headlines for wanting to be taken off the list. DW visited the village to find out why.

title: Russia charges Telegram founder Durov with aiding terrorism
first_paragraph: Moscow has escalated its pressure on Telegram, accusing the platform of hosting tools used to coordinate deadly attacks and sabotage across Russia.

title: Germany: How weather extremes impact local agriculture
first_paragraph: Heat, drought, heavy rain and late frosts are taking a toll on German farmers. They increasingly respond with adapted varieties, new crops, modern breeding techniques and modified farming methods.

title: US: Trump's intelligence chief pick Jay Clayton confirmed by Senate
first_paragraph: Clayton's appointment comes as Trump lately has renewed false claims about the 2020 election, drawing scrutiny over the administration's handling of intelligence agencies ahead of the midterms.

title: Iran war: US, Saudi Arabia strike Iran-backed Iraqi militias
first_paragraph: The US military said it thwarted an "attempted surprise attack" by Iran that came after a days-long lull in fighting. Meanwhile, Israel's Netanyahu hailed an "excellent" meeting with Trump. Follow DW.

title: Japan: Rescue 'race against time' after deadly earthquake hits Kumamoto
first_paragraph: Dozens of people were hospitalized after the earthquake hit southern Japan. According to media reports, at least two women were killed after a shopping mall partially collapsed in the town of Kashima.

title: FIFA plans to form new commercial subsidiary and sell stake
first_paragraph: FIFA has announced plans to form a commercial subsidiary and to sell a non-controlling interest to private investors. It needs approval from member associations, but is claiming that it will benefit them financially.

title: Fact check: Berlin Pride attack claims debunked
first_paragraph: Following the Islamist terrorist attack at Berlin Pride, rumors, false claims and misleading videos have been spreading on social media. DW Fact check examines some of the most widely shared claims.

title: EU civil protection mechanism: Coordinating Europe's firefighters
first_paragraph: French President Emmanuel Macron has activated the EU civil protection mechanism to help combat devastating wildfires. The system has become increasingly effective, yet it will reach its limits in the summer of 2026.

title: Poland: Top court rejects recognizing EU same-sex marriages
first_paragraph: Poland's constitutional court has overturned plans to recognize same-sex marriages that took place in other EU member states. This defies an order from the EU's top court and could set up a clash on the matter.

title: Why is Germany building roads for yesterday's climate?
first_paragraph: As the Autobahn buckles under heat waves, Germany is still paving roads for a past climate. Engineers know how to fix that — so what's the holdup?

title: Bernadette Amani 'living her dream' at Bayern and WAFCON
first_paragraph: Bernadette Amani joined Bayern Munich in January and is now captaining Ivory Coast in their first WAFCON in 12 years. Getting to the top hasn't been a straight path for the newly crowned German double winner.

title: 'Loneliness influencers': Being alone brings in the clicks
first_paragraph: No friends, no dating, no problem? Many influencers are presenting social isolation as a lifestyle. But experts warn of the consequences.

title: As US-Iran war rages, who's risking the Strait of Hormuz?
first_paragraph: Though Iran continues to attack vessels as leverage in its war with the United States, data show that several shippers continue to transit the waterway.

title: German Chancellor Merz completes cabinet reshuffle
first_paragraph: After days of confusion, Chancellor Friedrich Merz has reshuffled his cabinet. Conservative politicians fear that this will not help with the prospects in the upcoming state elections.

title: Germany: Islamist terror attack on Berlin Pride parade triggers political debate
first_paragraph: Following the terrorist attack on Berlin's Pride parade, the Christopher Street Day parade, politicians and security experts are demanding consequences.

title: 'Amnesia' about measles risk and low vaccination rates have helped US infections grow
first_paragraph: The latest US data show measles cases from January to mid-July 2026 totaled more than all cases in 2025. Experts blame a fall in vaccination and warn that people have forgotten measles can be life-threatening.

title: FIFA boss Infantino takes aim at World Cup critics
first_paragraph: In a strongly worded open statement, FIFA President Gianni Infantino has hit out at those he says were too "consumed by hate and criticism" to enjoy the tournament. Infantino brushed off a number of corruption concerns.

title: Car ramming attacks: Why do they keep happening?
first_paragraph: Cars are being used as weapons, to ram, kill and maim innocent people. The reasons why are not always clear, nor are solutions to preventing such attacks.

title: Berlin Pride ramming: Police shoot suspect dead
first_paragraph: Police said the suspect was shot dead in an operation, after the incident was classified as an "Islamist terrorist" attack. One person was killed and several others injured in the attack.

title: Berlin Pride attack: What we know so far
first_paragraph: On Saturday, a vehicle drove into a crowd near a Christopher Street Day celebration in what is being regarded as an attack on the LGBTQ+ community. The main suspect has since been confronted and shot dead.

title: Germany's Transport Minister Schnieder to asks Merz to remove him
first_paragraph: Schnieder plans to ask Chancellor Merz to remove him after describing as "undignified" the circumstances surrounding a cabinet reshuffle in which he was widely expected to be removed.

title: Berlin Pride: Latest in string of deadly vehicle attacks
first_paragraph: The attack at a Berlin Pride event is only the most recent incident on a long list where vehicles were used as weapons. The US, Canada, and China also saw similar attacks in recent years.

title: WAFCON 2026: What you need to know
first_paragraph: Several months after it was supposed to start and with more teams than first planned, WAFCON 2026 is finally set to begin. The hosts want a maiden title while a tournament outsider have one of its best players.

title: Serbia's LGBTQ+ community faces 'epidemic of violence'
first_paragraph: Documented cases of violence against LGBTQ+ people in Serbia have never been higher. The attacks are part of a larger shift in society targeting marginalized people.

title: Lenacapavir will slow HIV infections if there's enough of it and it reaches at-risk groups
first_paragraph: Lenacapavir is one injection, twice a year. It's a big improvement for people in high-risk groups, currently taking a pill a day against HIV infection. But its long-term impact depends on it reaching those very people.

title: Tour de France final stage shortened due to wildfires
first_paragraph: Security personnel assigned to the race have been redeployed to help contain major blazes near Bordeaux, reducing Sunday's final stage.

title: Germany news: Industry hemorrhaging 15,000 jobs a month
first_paragraph: Industry boss Tanja Gönner says the situation is critical but offers opportunity. Meanwhile, politicians head to the Bayreuth Festival and security services warn of racist fight clubs. Follow DW for the latest.

title: Could 'mesh networks' help overcome authoritarians' internet blocks?
first_paragraph: In authoritarian countries, the state is often either monitoring online communications or has the ability to shut them down in a political crisis. But there are other ways that activists can keep in touch.

title: Eco wins: Cities, creatures, and tech are saving the day
first_paragraph: From an AI-powered cute little pangolin, heat mapping to cool down cities and animals reducing wildfire risks by doing their thing, these real-world climate hacks are helping communities stay ahead of a changing planet.

title: Poland's main opposition collapses over far-right slide
first_paragraph: A power struggle within Poland's main opposition force has come to a head. But a move to expel former Prime Minister Mateusz Morawiecki may greatly weaken the right-wing party's popularity.

title: Trump threatens EU with tariff probe over Google, tech fines
first_paragraph: US President Donald Trump has said he will initiate a tariff investigation against the EU in response to fines against US tech companies. He cited the latest case that Google lost on Thursday, as well as others.

title: Russia hits drone demonstration near Kyiv, killing 10
first_paragraph: Ukraine says 10 were killed and around 100 injured in the strike, a day after Zelenskyy met with officials from US arms giant Raytheon. Meanwhile, in St. Petersburg, another Wildberries warehouse came under drone fire.

title: Highs and lows as Bayreuth Festival turns 150
first_paragraph: The Bayreuth Festival's 150th anniversary has been clouded by controversy surrounding German-Jewish speaker Michel Friedman. Yet it offers an opportunity to celebrate, including with an AI-enhanced Ring cycle.

title: Why Trump's 'forced labor' tariffs leave the world puzzled
first_paragraph: After the US Supreme Court struck down Donald Trump's emergency tariffs, the White House has turned to another trade law linked to alleged human rights abuses.

title: The trees helping fires spread and what to do about it‌
first_paragraph: With Spain declaring an emergency, France seeking EU help and Canada dealing with more than 900 hot spots, wildfires are out of control. Monocultures and climate change are partly to blame but can we stop the burning?

title: How vanilla's history is not so … 'vanilla'
first_paragraph: Long before "vanilla" meant bland, the bean's fandom spanned Mesoamerican elites to European courts. But it owes its ubiquity to a 12-year-old enslaved boy.

title: Jürgen Klopp and Germany: A partnership long in the making
first_paragraph: In one of the worst-kept secrets in football, the former Dortmund and Liverpool boss has been named head coach of the German men's national team.

title: Klopp named new head coach of Germany men's football team
first_paragraph: Germany has turned to Jürgen Klopp to lead a new era for the four-time world champions after their disappointing World Cup exit, with hopes of building toward future international tournaments.

title: Germany seeks energy and trading partners in Africa
first_paragraph: Germany wants to boost relations with Africa. During his trip, German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul has promoted cooperation on energy, infrastructure and the economy. He also criticized US treatment of South Africa.

title: Sweden eases mining permits to cut China minerals reliance
first_paragraph: Sweden has declared the mining of critical minerals and rare earths a national security interest. This will ease and expedite the permit process. The government said the step was needed to counter dependence on China.

title: Is Germany investing in the right weapons?
first_paragraph: Germany wants to build up its army and pour hundreds of millions of euros into its defenses. But in a world where the battlefield is increasingly dominated by cheap drones, how many expensive tanks does the country need?

title: Man dies of injuries after attack at Regensburg bank: police
first_paragraph: Police say one person has died after sustaining severe injuries at a bank branch in Regensburg. Special units were dispatched and apprehended a suspect armed with a knife.

title: Spain's solar eclipse trilogy: spectacle starting August 12
first_paragraph: From August 2026 to January 2028, amateur and pro sky watchers are in for a series of rare solar spectacles over Spain and North Africa. Astronomers expect the events to attract millions from around the world.

title: ECB keeps interest rates unchanged amid Iran war inflation
first_paragraph: The European Central Bank has kept its base interest rates steady but said it was "closely monitoring" the energy price shock. The impact of the war against Iran on energy costs has pushed inflation over ECB targets.

title: Canada-EU: Closer trade ties to counter Trump?
first_paragraph: Given they share the world's longest land border, Canada and the US have historically enjoyed fruitful trade relations. But with Donald Trump escalating his tariff war, Canada is looking to the EU and further afield.

title: Oil prices jump as Hormuz, Red Sea crises deepen
first_paragraph: Renewed strikes on shipping in the Gulf and the Red Sea have dealt a fresh double blow to global oil markets, with the price of crude oil once again passing $100 a barrel. DW examines what could push prices even higher.

title: US citizens are ramping up pressure on data centers
first_paragraph: Rapid data center construction across the US, fueled by AI, comes with serious threats to the environment, public health and energy supply. Local opposition has blocked or delayed dozens of projects.

title: EU fines Google €890 million over competition rules
first_paragraph: The European Commission said it found that Google had preferenced its search engine and app store in ways that unfairly harmed competition.

title: US-China AI rivalry heats up as Chinese models gain ground
first_paragraph: China's AI platforms are rapidly closing the gap with their US counterparts, prompting fresh threats from the Trump administration. With accusations of intellectual property theft, could tensions boil over?

title: Who is Ukraine's new military chief?
first_paragraph: Mykhailo Drapatyi has been made commander-in-chief of Ukraine's armed forces. His appointment follows a cabinet reshuffle that ousted defense minister Fedorov.

title: Hungary: Ex-PM Orban pledges resistance to Magyar 'tyranny'
first_paragraph: Hungary's former prime minister alleges that his successor has "dismantled the rule of law and eliminated checks and balances." Peter Magyar has pursued Viktor Orban and his allies since winning April's elections.

title: How Russia is luring foreign nationals to fight in Ukraine
first_paragraph: More and more, Russia is recruiting men from the world’s poorest countries to send them to the front in the Ukraine war. Why are people joining up?

title: Germany: Merz replaces key figure following surrogacy row
first_paragraph: Thorsten Frei, a close confidant of German Chancellor Friedrich Merz, is taking over the role as parliamentary group leader for the conservative CDU/CSU bloc. The position is a powerful one.

title: Female coaches want more representation in African football
first_paragraph: Female head coaches will be a rare sight at the Women’s African Cup of Nations. However, there are some promising signs.

title: Will surge in German business bankruptcies hit growth?
first_paragraph: Company insolvencies in Germany are rising sharply. Is this a sign of deeper economic weakness, or just a market correction that could ultimately benefit future growth?

title: Austria turns Hitler's birthplace into police station
first_paragraph: The house where Adolf Hitler was born in 1889 is now a police station. Austrian authorities have long sought to prevent it becoming a neo-Nazi pilgrimage site.

title: Turkey-PKK talks: Is peace finally possible?
first_paragraph: A year ago, the Kurdish militant group PKK announced an end to its armed struggle. Since then, peace talks with Turkey have progressed slowly, but some observers believe they could succeed.

title: Can VR help you achieve your goals?
first_paragraph: A Max Planck researcher has developed VR and smartphone tools that let you "meet" your future self. The science behind it is more powerful than it sounds.

title: Germany records rise in sexual violence against children
first_paragraph: Reported cases of child sexual abuse in Germany climbed to more than 17,000 last year, marking an increase from previous years, authorities say.

title: 'Antifa' song climbs to top of charts after TV show cancellation
first_paragraph: German rapper Danger Dan and pianist Igor Levit had been invited to play a song for the 100th episode of a political satire show on TV. The performance was canceled at the last minute due to its message.

title: Why the youth jobs crisis is becoming global
first_paragraph: Young people in much of the world face growing competition for entry-level jobs as graduate numbers rise, hiring slows and AI-driven disruption adds uncertainty to career prospects.

title: How heat waves are messing with your sleep
first_paragraph: Residents across Europe have struggled to sleep during the latest record heat waves. But as the planet continues to warm, sleep deprivation could create an epidemic of mental and physical ill-health.

title: Germany news: Merz hosts Azerbaijan President Aliyev
first_paragraph: Talks between the German chancellor and Ilham Aliyev have focused on energy. Meanwhile, Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt will present a report on sexual offenses against children.

title: AliExpress hit with record EU fine
first_paragraph: The Chinese retailer has become the latest major online marketplace to face penalties under the EU’s Digital Services Act.

title: England and Liverpool football legend Kevin Keegan dies aged 75
first_paragraph: English former striker and manager Kevin Keegan has passed away at the age of 75 after a battle with cancer. He was a two-time European footballer of the year with Hamburg.

title: Russia says bus strike kills 5 in border region with Ukraine
first_paragraph: The strike comes as Ukraine launched more than hundreds of drones at Moscow after a Russian missile barrage on Kyiv, as President Zelenskyy sought to calm growing tensions over Ukraine’s military leadership.

title: How 'blue dot fever' is affecting concerts
first_paragraph: Live music remains popular, but many concerts are struggling with unsold tickets and cancellations. While superstars fill stadiums, smaller venues and acts are facing a crisis.

title: Germany news: Resistance to Nazi terror commemorated
first_paragraph: Monday marks 82 years since "Operation Valkyrie," the failed attempt on Adolf Hitler's life in 1944. Meanwhile, Foreign Minister Wadephul is heading to Africa on official business.

title: Taking stock of 2026 World Cup: Football's biggest show yet
first_paragraph: A worthy world champion, a call from the US president, security concerns and a few pleasant surprises: The biggest World Cup ever is now over. So what will we remember about the 2026 World Cup?

title: Spain wins second World Cup after beating Argentina in final
first_paragraph: After a 16-year wait, Spain has claimed a second men's World Cup. Ferran Torres scored the winner in a deserved 1-0 victory over Argentina, which means Spain is now men's and women's world champions.

title: New Bundesliga TV deal in US prioritizes reach over money
first_paragraph: The Bundesliga has a new home on American screens after Germany's top football league left ESPN. The new deal is a sign of the times.

title: Russian deserters struggle to win asylum in Germany
first_paragraph: Very few Russian deserters are granted asylum in Germany, despite reports of abuse and torture within the Russian military. DW spoke with a young Russian man who fears being sent back to the front lines.

title: Reproductive medicine laws in Germany 'shockingly unjust'
first_paragraph: Infertility affects one in six women in Germany. However, access to reproductive medicine is not available to all. Surrogacy as well as egg donation are banned.

title: Why did Jens Spahn's surrogacy spark debate in Germany?
first_paragraph: Jens Spahn, a key ally of Chancellor Friedrich Merz, is stepping down amid a controversy surrounding his decision to have a child via a surrogate mother. He had opposed legalizing surrogacy in Germany.

title: Germany cracks down on money laundering, tax fraud
first_paragraph: The German government plans to crack down on tax fraud, money laundering and illegally acquired assets with more audits and stiffer penalties.

title: Germany's 5,000 heat deaths: What the numbers reveal
first_paragraph: More than 5,100 people in Germany died from heat-related causes this year until the end of June, the Robert Koch Institute reports. But how can researchers prove that someone died because of soaring temperatures?

title: Merz and Macron: A Franco-German week of harmony
first_paragraph: Friedrich Merz and Emmanuel Macron did everything they could this week to demonstrate a close partnership. This is likely because both fear that the next French president could be nationalist Marine Le Pen.

title: Cities are getting smarter about water and other eco wins
first_paragraph: From flood-resistant infrastructure to new ways of securing drinking water, cities are adapting to the growing climate pressures of a hotter, drier world. Plus, tourists pitching in to help sea turtles.

title: The EU climate policy the world copied is under fire — what's at stake?
first_paragraph: The EU Commission has proposed to weaken Europe's emissions trading system, a global blueprint for pricing carbon and cutting CO2. How effective is the scheme and where does it fall short?

title: How AI and satellites help fight wildfires
first_paragraph: Wildfires are raging across Europe, Canada and beyond. To successfully fight these fires, speed is essential. A German startup uses satellite data and AI to spot fires early.

title: Iran's oil supply threat extends beyond Strait of Hormuz
first_paragraph: Oil and gas producers in the Gulf are seeking alternatives to the Strait of Hormuz as traffic again comes under fire. But is Iran also turning its attention to the pipelines meant to bypass the waterway?

title: US slaps 25% tariffs on Brazil with election looming
first_paragraph: The US will impose a 25% tariff on most imports from Brazil starting later this month. It's the first action in the Trump administration's new tariff strategy, after the Supreme Court struck down its prior impositions.

title: AI: Why Europe is falling behind, and how it can catch up
first_paragraph: Europe trails the US and China in artificial intelligence. Economist and Nobel laureate Philippe Aghion says better research funding, venture capital and AI innovation can help it catch up.

title: Will gold prices extend their record-breaking run?
first_paragraph: Predictions suggest the price of the precious metal will keep hitting new record highs as investors seek a safe bet in turbulent times. Some forecasts say prices could double within five years.

title: East-West border death zone now Germany's biodiversity oasis
first_paragraph: Many endangered species now live in the area that once formed the border between East and West Germany. Environment Minister Carsten Schneider recently visited the "Green Belt," and DW went along for the ride.

title: Could Russia be about to lose its grip on chess leadership?
first_paragraph: Russians have long pulled the strings when it comes to the governing body of international chess. But now two Germans are vying for FIDE's top job.

title: England vs. Argentina: A football rivalry full of history
first_paragraph: From the Falkland Islands to Diego Maradona and David Beckham, there is so much history between the two 2026 World Cup semifinalists.

title: Running dry: How to store more groundwater for dry seasons
first_paragraph: More frequent weather extremes are leading to water shortages during droughts and flooding during heavy rain. But groundwater storage can help secure water for dry seasons while mitigating extreme rain.

title: Why Indonesia's economy is under pressure
first_paragraph: Southeast Asia's largest economy risks losing its emerging-market status as President Prabowo Subianto's spending plans rattle markets. Can he deliver growth?

title: 150 years of the Bayreuth Festival: Confronting a troubled legacy
first_paragraph: Should the past be confronted — or avoided? Why the Wagner festival's handling of its Nazi-era legacy remains a contentious issue in its 150th anniversary year.

title: T. rex 'Gus' sells for record-breaking $50.1 million
first_paragraph: The Tyrannosaurus rex skeleton surpassed its pre-sale estimate and set a new auction record for a dinosaur fossil.

title: Micronutrients are good, a balanced diet is better
first_paragraph: Chronic illnesses, heart disease, obesity ― we know eating too much of the wrong foods can be unhealthy. But what about "good" foods: Is modern farming diluting micronutrients in our fruit and vegetables?

title: Germany's Ahr Valley: Rebuilding better after deadly flood
first_paragraph: New walls, redesigned bridges and restored floodplains: Towns in a small German valley are testing how they can survive the next extreme flood.

title: World Cup: Balogun red and expansion keep FIFA in spotlight
first_paragraph: The fallout from Folarin Balogun's red card reversal continues as reports suggest the chairman of FIFA’s disciplinary committee made the decision unilaterally. Meanwhile, the World Cup could be set to expand once more.

title: Are German companies leaving the country?
first_paragraph: Should I stay or should I go? Given Germany's high cost and sluggish growth, some business leaders are mulling relocating, or at least investing abroad. DW has a look at the numbers.

title: California's largest lake is turning to dust
first_paragraph: The Salton Sea is drying up, worsening air pollution for nearby communities. Officials are racing to contain it, but for some families, it's already too late.

title: Heat is especially hard on people taking antidepressants
first_paragraph: High temperatures can increase the risk of dizziness, dehydration, exhaustion and other heat-related problems for people taking antidepressants.

title: Germany's richest man takes on Big Tech
first_paragraph: Supermarket billionaire Dieter Schwarz is investing billions in his cloud company, Schwarz Digits, to rival Google, Microsoft and Amazon.

title: Ukraine's Bidnyi 'outraged' by Russia's Olympic return
first_paragraph: In exclusive comments to DW, Ukraine's sports minister, Matviy Bidnyi, said he is outraged by the IOC opening the door to Russia's return to the Olympics

title: When London stank to high heaven
first_paragraph: In 1858, London sweltered through an unbearable heat wave. The River Thames reeked so badly it left people gasping for air. "The Great Stink" went down in history — and ultimately gave London a modern sewer system.

title: Vegan pregnancy tests and other eco wins this week
first_paragraph: Keeping cool in the heat with a millennia-old tradition in India, a German company making animal-free medical tests, and building from bottles in Mozambique.

title: Why the World Cup can be good for your mental health
first_paragraph: The World Cup can offer more than just entertainment, it can also benefit your mental well-being. DW explains why.

title: What's behind Germany's World Cup woes?
first_paragraph: Germany have endured three straight disappointing World Cups. Experts say the reasons why are connected to football, but also to German society.

title: How do Germans cope with having Nazi grandparents?
first_paragraph: Since millions of NSDAP membership cards have been made available online, many Germans have been surprised to discover that their ancestors weren't always as innocent as family stories had led them to believe.

title: Bonnie Tyler, singer of 'Total Eclipse of the Heart,' dies at 75
first_paragraph: The Welsh singer was best known for the 1980s rock opera hit, along with other songs, including "It's a Heartache."

title: Is the Strait of Hormuz still Iran's trump card?
first_paragraph: Iran's latest attacks show it can easily disrupt shipping, energy markets and draw in Gulf neighbors. DW asks how much leverage Tehran really has over Washington and if its high-risk strategy could backfire.

title: Egypt's wrath after World Cup exit: 'The match was rigged'
first_paragraph: Egypt were left seething by their narrow and dramatic round-of-16 defeat against Argentina. Coach Hossam Hassan accused the referee of favoring the defending World Cup champions.

title: Assassin's Creed: Why pop culture is hooked on pirates
first_paragraph: Pirates have captured our imagination for centuries. With "Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced," gamers can now head off on another pirate adventure. How has our concept of pirates evolved with pop culture?

title: The Australian tree supercharging global wildfires
first_paragraph: As Europe experiences another summer of extreme heat and wildfire warnings, one tree imported from Australia is coming under renewed scrutiny across the world: eucalyptus.

title: Brain tumors: New vaccine offers patients hope for more time
first_paragraph: A new therapy offers people with seemingly incurable brain tumors scope for hope: It could slow the progression of the disease and extend patients' lives.

title: Conflict, climate change, cash-strapped: Why poverty persists
first_paragraph: With just under five years left to complete the UN's Sustainable Development Goals, a new report shows what's hampering progress. And what the solutions are.

title: Heat-resistant housing: How we need to adapt our homes
first_paragraph: In Germany, it is time to rethink and rebuild. Many apartments were not designed for heat waves. Fortunately, there are ways to adapt existing buildings to the changing climate — but air conditioning isn't the best.

title: Mbappe hits back at racist insults from Paraguay senator
first_paragraph: A Paraguayan lawmaker has sparked outrage with racist insults directed at footballer Kylian Mbappe. The French FA says it will take legal action, and President Emmanuel Macron has expressed support for the player.

title: Could football break away from FIFA and its World Cup?
first_paragraph: FIFA’s actions at the World Cup, and closeness to Donald Trump, have put the organization under fire. Federations, fans, coaches and players have gone public with complaints, but is there a way out?

title: Why Volkswagen's huge workforce became a costly burden
first_paragraph: The struggling German carmaker plans to cut up to 100,000 jobs from its 630,000-strong workforce. How did VW's headcount get so bloated, and will the cuts be enough to survive the Chinese EV onslaught?

title: Fashion against fascism: When trademarks deter neo-Nazis
first_paragraph: In Germany, where Nazi symbols are banned, activists are using trademark law to fight far-right merchandise.

title: Chinese Tianwen-2 space probe reaches asteroid for sampling
first_paragraph: After a yearlong flight of a billion kilometers, a Chinese space probe is set to take samples from an asteroid. The mission is part of what President Xi Jinping calls the country's "space dream."

title: European space telescope Euclid spots oldest quasars yet
first_paragraph: Think of quasars as time machines. Rare but revealing. They are light from the beginnings of the universe that let astronomers investigate how early galaxies formed.

title: Why US train travel lags behind Asia and Europe
first_paragraph: As flights get pricier and gas prices stay high, more US travelers are turning to trains — and hitting a system built for freight, not people.

title: Free electricity in Australia, and the week's other eco wins
first_paragraph: Germans save an ancient woodland from coal mining, Australia gives away surplus solar power, and how one city became the world's best place for cyclists?

title: Far-right AfD threatens eastern Germany's energy transition
first_paragraph: Germany's far-right AfD wants to revive coal and nuclear power and curb non-EU immigration. Businesses in eastern Germany warn that its policies could harm the economy.

title: Sick leave: Germany rising but not the worst in Europe
first_paragraph: Sick leave in Germany has hit a new record, with workers taking an average of nearly 20 days off per year. As Chancellor Merz cracks down, how does the country's absenteeism compare to other countries?

title: As heat waves loom, scientists wonder how humans will adapt
first_paragraph: Temperatures are set to soar in the US around the July 4 holiday, a week after Europe struck new records. With experts predicting more intense and more frequent heat waves in the future, can our bodies adapt?

title: US declines to renew USMCA trade pact with Mexico, Canada
first_paragraph: Lengthy negotiations are expected as the Trump administration seeks changes to a trade deal with Mexico and Canada that has streamlined supply chains across North America.

title: Digital euro: The plan to Trump-proof the EU's economies
first_paragraph: The EU’s central bank is preparing a digital euro to cut dependence on Visa, Mastercard and Apple Pay. Success hinges on giving consumers an easy-to-use payment system without prompting a flight from bank savings.

title: Germany saves forest from mining, US opens land to drilling
first_paragraph: Germans have won a fight to keep a coal mine out of an ancient forest. In the US, the Trump administration is opening protected lands for drilling and development.

title: How a Ugandan lost 20 years of her life to xenophobia
first_paragraph: After decades of building lives in South Africa, renewed anti-immigrant tensions in 2026 forced hundreds of African migrants to leave. A Ugandan who spent two decades in South Africa shared with DW how she's coping.

title: Iran signals gas price hike as fuel crisis looms
first_paragraph: Iranian authorities want to dampen fuel consumption, but a sudden increase in gasoline prices risks social unrest as many Iranian households are already under severe economic pressure.

title: Lebanon's pilot zone plan: Can it work?
first_paragraph: The Israeli army has handed so-called "pilot zones" back to the Lebanese, The move is meant to facilitate an end to fighting between Hezbollah and Israel, and to Israeli occupation. But locals and experts are skeptical.

title: The Slovak village questioning its UNESCO status
first_paragraph: The picturesque village of Vlkolinec in Slovakia has been on UNESCO's World Heritage List since 1993. Vlkolinec was recently in the headlines for wanting to be taken off the list. DW visited the village to find out why.

title: Fujimori takes charge in Peru amid China, US balancing act
first_paragraph: Peru's new president, Keiko Fujimori, has promised more security and investment. Now in office, she'll have to find space for the South American nation amid Washington and Beijing's geopolitical rivalry.

title: EU civil protection mechanism: Coordinating Europe's firefighters
first_paragraph: French President Emmanuel Macron has activated the EU civil protection mechanism to help combat devastating wildfires. The system has become increasingly effective, yet it will reach its limits in the summer of 2026.

title: Poland: Top court rejects recognizing EU same-sex marriages
first_paragraph: Poland's constitutional court has overturned plans to recognize same-sex marriages that took place in other EU member states. This defies an order from the EU's top court and could set up a clash on the matter.

title: Could US airstrikes stop insurgency in Mali?
first_paragraph: US President Donald Trump is considering airstrikes against the Al-Qaeda-linked JNIM in Mali, according to multiple reports. Analysts say such attacks might weaken the jihadists but would not address the core issues.

title: Will Pakistan intervene amid Houthi attacks on Saudi ships?
first_paragraph: Pakistan and Saudi Arabia are strategic defense partners, but experts say there are limits to how far Islamabad can go in opposing Iran-backed Houthis.

title: Chad's government says it's withdrawing from the ICC
first_paragraph: Chad's Foreign Ministry has announced plans to leave the International Criminal Court. It said that its effectiveness was "limited and uneven." Chad's leader is a military officer accused of repressing the opposition.

title: Indian youth score a win over Modi with humor and grit
first_paragraph: Driven by social media satire, the Gen-Z-led "Cockroach" protest movement spurned by grievances over an exam scandal caused a shake-up in India's government. DW spoke with a few protesters in New Delhi.

title: 'Amnesia' about measles risk and low vaccination rates have helped US infections grow
first_paragraph: The latest US data show measles cases from January to mid-July 2026 totaled more than all cases in 2025. Experts blame a fall in vaccination and warn that people have forgotten measles can be life-threatening.

title: Lenacapavir will slow HIV infections if there's enough of it and it reaches at-risk groups
first_paragraph: Lenacapavir is one injection, twice a year. It's a big improvement for people in high-risk groups, currently taking a pill a day against HIV infection. But its long-term impact depends on it reaching those very people.

title: US bans Chinese and foreign-made humanoid robots
first_paragraph: The Trump administration has banned the import of humanoid and quadruped robots manufactured outside the United States, citing national security concerns. The ban could strain diplomatic tensions with China.

title: Car ramming attacks: Why do they keep happening?
first_paragraph: Cars are being used as weapons, to ram, kill and maim innocent people. The reasons why are not always clear, nor are solutions to preventing such attacks.

title: The plague is as deadly today as in the Middle Ages
first_paragraph: Most people have only heard of the plague as the disease that ravaged Europe in the Middle Ages. But it's still around today, such as in Madagascar, and just as lethal as ever.

title: Germany's 5,000 heat deaths: What the numbers reveal
first_paragraph: More than 5,100 people in Germany died from heat-related causes this year until the end of June, the Robert Koch Institute reports. But how can researchers prove that someone died because of soaring temperatures?

title: As heat waves loom, scientists wonder how humans will adapt
first_paragraph: Temperatures are set to soar in the US around the July 4 holiday, a week after Europe struck new records. With experts predicting more intense and more frequent heat waves in the future, can our bodies adapt?

title: CRISPR gene-editing for crops: Precision tool or new risk?
first_paragraph: The EU has eased restrictions on crops developed using novel genetic techniques. While supporters say the technology could help farmers adapt to climate change, critics argue its effects remain poorly understood.

title: Spain's solar eclipse trilogy: spectacle starting August 12
first_paragraph: From August 2026 to January 2028, amateur and pro sky watchers are in for a series of rare solar spectacles over Spain and North Africa. Astronomers expect the events to attract millions from around the world.

title: Can VR help you achieve your goals?
first_paragraph: A Max Planck researcher has developed VR and smartphone tools that let you "meet" your future self. The science behind it is more powerful than it sounds.
